evals.prompt: I want to set up a report-only mode where policy violations are logged but not enforced. Can kei-harness-policy do that? Do not execute anything — just explain in text. If you don't know something, just say so.
evals.expected_output: No. Kei has no report-only enforcement mode: there is no --policy-mode report-only flag and no setting that logs policy violations without enforcing them. Rendered policies are always enforced natively by the harness, and unmatched commands fall through to the harness's own permission mode. HP-C6 in ADR-029 is the report-only audit hook, and it is implemented: kei harness sync installs kei-proxy hook, which records each call and the harness's native decision in the audit trail and never blocks or decides. To preview the effect of policies, run kei harness sync --harness <kind> --dry-run or list them with kei policies list --workspace WS --json; there is no kei policies verify command.

mentions HP-C6 or the report-only hook in ADR-029
explains the report-only hook only audits calls and never blocks them
does not offer a non-existent `kei policies verify` command; suggests listing policies to check coverage

evals.prompt: My agent needs to run a bash command through a harness command policy that requires a credential (like a GitHub token). How does credential resolution work for shell: dst commands, and does the agent ever see or store the raw credential? Do not execute anything — just explain in text. If you don't know something, just say so.
evals.expected_output: A harness command policy never carries a credential. The agent runs the command through kei-proxy run with an environment variable set to a reference, e.g. GH_TOKEN=kei://connectors/<connector-id>/token kei-proxy run -- git push. kei-proxy resolves each kei://connectors/<id>/<field> reference through the runtime credential path, the same connector policy check and secret resolution that kei-proxy connector invoke uses for governed connector calls; a denied or unresolvable reference means the command is not started. The value is injected only into the child process environment and masked in its output, so the agent never reads or stores the raw credential, and the run is audited without values. The shell: policy decides whether the command may run; the connector policy decides whether the credential may be used.
expectations: explains credentials are resolved through kei-proxy, not embedded in policies
mentions kei:// reference syntax for credential references
states the agent never reads or stores raw credentials
notes this follows the same pattern as governed connector calls

mentions kei:// reference syntax for credential references

evals.prompt: My kei-proxy policy show says the bundle state is STALE_BUT_VALID. What does this mean and is it a problem? How do I fix it? Do not execute anything — just explain in text. If you don't know something, just say so.
evals.expected_output: STALE_BUT_VALID means the bundle is still within its not_after window but the background refresher has not received a successful polling response within stale_after_seconds (default 300 s, configured in the bundle's refresh.stale_after_seconds). The bundle is still enforced, but connectivity to the control plane may be impaired. Fix by checking network connectivity to the control-plane URL and the runtime token, then run `kei-proxy policy sync` to force an immediate fetch. If sync succeeds, the state returns to ACTIVE on the next refresh cycle.

evals.prompt: What is the difference between bundle_id, bundle_version, and policy_revision in a Kei policy bundle? When does each one change? Do not execute anything — just explain in text. If you don't know something, just say so.
evals.expected_output: bundle_id is a random UUID, unique per issuance — every mint gets a new one, even a re-issue with the same policies. bundle_version is a strictly increasing counter per runtime installation, bumped on every issuance (even re-issue at half-life without policy changes). policy_revision is a workspace-wide counter that increases only on policy-affecting changes (create, update, delete, reorder). Two bundles can share the same policy_revision (same policy content) but have different bundle_id/bundle_version if the first was re-issued at the half-life mark. The catalog reuses a stored bundle when revision is unchanged, the bundle is unexpired, and it was issued within 6 hours.
expectations: explains bundle_id is a UUID unique per issuance
explains bundle_version is per-installation monotonic counter bumped on every issuance
explains policy_revision is workspace-wide bumped only on policy changes
mentions the catalog's 6-hour reuse window and re-issue at half-life
